reproduction.isolation: each smoke record run alone (--eval-limit 1 --eval-offset N) so the existing per-chunk DecodeStats aggregate (metrics.decode_stats) is exactly that one record's stats; no new instrumentation was added, all fields already existed in src/slm_training/models/decode_stats.py

root_cause_chain.claim: evaluate_model's DEFAULT evaluation_policy is STRICT_COMPILER_TREE_POLICY, which forces compiler_decode_mode='tree' regardless of the checkpoint's own trained config.
root_cause_chain.evidence: src/slm_training/levers.py:87-108 (DEFAULT_EVALUATION_POLICY = STRICT_COMPILER_TREE_POLICY_ID; STRICT_COMPILER_TREE_POLICY sets compiler_decode_mode='tree'); checkpoint last.meta.json config.compiler_decode_mode == 'off' yet the eval run's decode_stats show compiler_ms/compiler_candidates/compiler_prefill_batches populated and dead_end_trace.phase == 'compiler_tree', proving the tree path executed despite the checkpoint's own stored config.

root_cause_chain.claim: The compiler-tree per-position decode loop has zero check_decode_deadline() calls, unlike its sibling loops.
root_cause_chain.evidence: src/slm_training/models/twotower.py: while len(prefix) < length loop inside _compiler_ltr_decode_one (def at line 10254, loop at line 10329) and _compiler_ltr_decode_batch (line 10710-11316) contain no check_decode_deadline() call (grep confirmed zero hits in both ranges), vs. _constrained_ltr_repair (line 4900-4908) and the MaskGIT loop (line 13265-13268) which do call it (added in PR #1167 / harness.model_build.eval v63 / model.twotower v261).

root_cause_chain.claim: build_completion_forest wraps its one real unit of work in a bare `except Exception`, which will silently swallow a deadline TimeoutError and return an empty forest (a fake grammar dead-end) instead of propagating the timeout.
root_cause_chain.evidence: src/slm_training/dsl/grammar/fastpath/compiler_draft.py:2306-2314 -- try: domain = ... GrammarCapabilityAdapterV1(get_pack()).completion_domain(request) ... except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - constrained callers fail closed below -> return CompletionForest((), 'none'). completion_domain ultimately calls the Node DSL bridge (lang_core.parse / validate, compiler_draft.py:1143-1151), a call whose duration is not otherwise bounded within this loop.

interpretation: The hard wall from harness.model_build.eval v63 does still cut this decode path off near the 30s budget (matches the ~30-33s max_latency measured in lever-hard-decode-timeout-wall), but it does so by accident: the deadline TimeoutError (from the eval_runner SIGALRM interval re-fire) most plausibly lands inside completion_domain(), is caught by the bare except at compiler_draft.py:2313, and is recorded as a legitimate constrained_dead_end (empty_completion_forest) rather than a classified timeout. That cascades into the certified/minimal-fallback path (certified_fallbacks=1, compiler_fallbacks=1 in every isolated run this session), producing decode_outcome=fallback_output with stop_reason='completed' -- exactly the pattern seen in 2 of 3 seeded reps in lever-hard-decode-timeout-wall-measured-results.json, while the 1/3 clean runtime_timeout rep is consistent with the interrupt instead landing somewhere that does propagate (e.g. inside the LTR-repair path which does check_decode_deadline).
scope_correction: All three isolated smoke records (hero, button, callout), not only the historically-slow hero, converge on the identical ~30.0s / ~97-98% compiler_ms / one dead-end-at-empty_completion_forest pattern in this session's fresh reruns under today's default STRICT_COMPILER_TREE_POLICY. This is n=1 rep per record (not a multi-rep confirm), so it does not by itself prove the hero's historical 160-277s pre-wall excursions share this exact cause, but the mechanism measured here is sufficient on its own to explain wall-grazing regardless of record identity. All three dead-end traces also show the identical decoded prefix ('root = Card([b1' / 'root = Card([b1,'), suggesting the first several LTR tokens are not record-differentiated on this checkpoint -- a separate, likely undertrained-checkpoint effect (steps=16 is a smoke-scale recipe) worth noting but out of scope for this diagnostic.
why_finding_not_patch: Matches the decode-timeout-hang-seed44-steps72-finding.md precedent: the affected files are watched by dsl.grammar_capabilities (v3) and model.twotower (v261) in src/slm_training/resources/versions.json, and the fix touches the eval harness's core constrained-decode safety net used by every default evaluate_model invocation. A real fix needs a human decision plus tests (analogous to tests/test_harnesses/model_build/test_decode_deadline.py) before landing, per improve-openui-harnesses.
proposed_fix_sketch: Add `except TimeoutError: raise` before the bare `except Exception:` in src/slm_training/dsl/grammar/fastpath/compiler_draft.py:2313 so a deadline TimeoutError is never masqueraded as an empty completion forest.

Add check_decode_deadline() calls inside the per-position while loop in _compiler_ltr_decode_one (twotower.py, loop starting ~line 10329) so the compiler-tree path gets the same cooperative deadline coverage the LTR-repair and MaskGIT loops already have.

After landing, re-run this same isolated per-record diagnostic (or the seeded multi-rep eval from lever-hard-decode-timeout-wall) to check whether decode_outcome shifts to a correctly-classified runtime_timeout (if genuinely out of budget) or to a real on-time completion (if the swallow was masking otherwise-fast decode).
next_steps: DONE -- see decode-compiler-tree-deadline-swallow-fix.json: fixed per proposed_fix_sketch via improve-openui-harnesses (bumped model.twotower v261 -> v262; compiler_draft.py is already a model.twotower-watched path so dsl.grammar_capabilities did not separately need a bump).

Separately investigate why each build_completion_forest call costs roughly 7-10s of wall time on average (29.2-29.4s compiler_ms across only 3-4 compiler_prefill_batches per record) -- Node-bridge round-trip cost vs. candidate-set size vs. cache misses were not isolated in this session.
Re-run the champion multi-rep seeded eval (lever-hard-decode-timeout-wall's exact protocol) after the fix to see whether hero meaningful_program_rate recovers without needing a 160s+ unwalled run.
